senses.sense_definition: The lower division of the seven liberal arts in medieval universities, comprising grammar, logic, and rhetoric.

examples.text: In medieval European universities, every undergraduate student was expected to master the <w>trivium</w> before advancing to higher studies.
The traditional curriculum paired the <w>trivium</w> with the four mathematical arts known as the quadrivium.

senses.sense_definition: A singular piece of trivia; a minor fact or matter of little value or importance.

examples.text: He dismissed the minor historical discrepancy as a mere <w>trivium</w> unworthy of serious debate.
The author included an interesting <w>trivium</w> about the author's eccentric daily routine in the footnote.

senses.sense_definition: The three anterior ambulacra of echinoderms, considered collectively.

examples.text: The marine biologist examined the sea star's <w>trivium</w> to assess its anatomical development.
In echinoderm anatomy, the <w>trivium</w> is distinguished clearly from the bivium.
